turn_1_riskmix.user_query: Walk me through the clinic risk mix
turn_1_riskmix.ai_message: The attributed panel of 200 splits with 60 in the high tier, the remainder across rising and low. What moved this refresh: remote-monitoring trends and utilization patterns pushed more weight into the high tier, while the social-need screens keep transport as the most common non-clinical driver. Every tier assignment shows its top reasons, and the trend line per refresh is what lets you see the mix move before the measure period closes — the drill-down goes from this clinic view to a ranked patient worklist with risk reasons and open gaps per patient.

turn_2_gaps.user_query: Which care gaps are still open?
turn_2_gaps.ai_message: 80 care-gap tasks are open against the measure set — overdue follow-ups, screenings not completed, and monitoring enrollments that never started — while 51 closed in the window. Each open gap traces to its patient, its measure, and the outreach task carrying it, so closure is tracked through to the booked, kept visit rather than stopping at 'letter sent'. The closure pace is the finding: tasks open faster than they close, and the open set skews toward the same high-tier patients driving the risk mix shift.

signal_closure.user_query: How are we trending on care-gap closure?
signal_closure.ai_message: Closure is running behind creation: 51 tasks closed in the window while 80 remain open, so the backlog grows each refresh. The closures that do land split across confirmed visits, completed screenings, and enrollment assists — and they trace end-to-end, gap to task to kept visit. The lever that moves this fastest is the scheduling loop: gaps feed outreach, outreach books visits, and the reminder engine keeps them from turning into no-shows.

q_telehealth_trend.user_query: What is our telehealth share trend?
q_telehealth_trend.ai_message: Telehealth carries 54 percent of visits in the current window. For a panel with hour-plus drives, that share is an access measure as much as a modality stat: every converted visit is a trip not wasted and a slot more likely kept. The share is reported by clinic and week on the same dashboard as confirmations and no-shows, so the quality program can see whether the reminder engine's telehealth offers are actually landing.

q_sdoh_coverage.user_query: What is our social-need screening coverage?
q_sdoh_coverage.ai_message: 200 screenings are on file across the five core domains — food, housing, transportation, utilities, and safety — which puts screening coverage at the full attributed panel. Coverage is the quality measure; what the answers change is the plan: transport positives steer visits toward telehealth and mobile outreach, and the positives feed the risk tier so social need shows up in the same worklist as clinical risk rather than in a separate binder.

q_benchmark.user_query: Compare our measures against county benchmarks
q_benchmark.ai_message: The benchmark view sets the clinic against its county baselines from the public datasets — CDC PLACES prevalence, the social vulnerability index, and rurality codes — the same comparison step the population-health dashboard runs at every scope. Where the clinic beats its county baseline, that difference is the grant-report evidence; where it trails, the gap list says which patients close it. All public sources are labelled, and the county data never identifies a patient.
